utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Madam Registrar, will you call the place, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-97-24-A, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: May I please have the appearances of the parties. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Norul Rashid representing the Prosecutor, and with me, Your Honour, it is my pleasure to introduce to Your Honour a new addition to the appeals section Ms. Barbara Goy, and with us is our case manager, Ms. Sue Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Branko Lukic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Stakic, can you hear me and can you understand me in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I hear you, and I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. You may be seated. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is -- this is a Status Conference called in accordance with the Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. Our last Status Conference in this case was on the 18th of December, 2003. Mr. Stakic, do you have any issues to raise in relation to your detention? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for asking. I don't have anything in particular to bring up at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: No problems regarding your mental or physical well-being? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Well, if a person can feel well in prison, then I'm well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. You may sit down. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I turn to the pending matters in this appeal. I note that the accused resubmitted his appeal brief on the 8th of March, 2004, in accordance with the decision dated 23 February on the Prosecution's motion. Actually, the brief was submitted late in the evening of the 8th of March, so the registry logged it on the 9th of March, but I don't propose to dwell on that. Under the decision of 23 February, the Prosecution has 30 days in which to file its response, 30 days from March 9th is this Thursday, April the 8th. The Prosecution advised the Appeals Chamber this morning that they were filing today a motion for an extension of the page limits for the filing of their response brief. They are seeking an extension of about 30 pages. I understand that the Prosecution and the Court has a copy of that motion for myself and for the Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is correct Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So could they be handed in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May the registrar hand to Your Honour a copy of the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: The Defence has been provided with a copy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Has been provided. Thank you very much. I would like to turn to the Defence and ask them to indicate if they oppose the extension of page limit sought. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't oppose the extension of pages. Thank you very much. As the Prosecution's response brief is due on Thursday and in light of the indication by the Defence that it does not oppose the extension of page limit sought, I will do my best to dispose of the motion as soon as possible. May I turn to the Prosecution. Again, I -- Ms. Rashid, I assume the Prosecution is planning to file its brief on time regardless of the outcome of the motion on extension of pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, absolutely. We will file it on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you so much. That is good. With regard to Mr. Stakic's motion under Rule 115, I have been informed by OLAD that the B/C/S documents attached to the motion have been translated and will be given to Mr. Lukic today. If they have not been given already. Have they been given to you already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I received them actually -- probably they were provided on Saturday because I found it yesterday in my locker. It's arranged, but I couldn't reach anybody in OLAD. So -- otherwise, they will be submitted. I just want to emphasise that eight documents have not been translated yet. I -- I indicated it in my letter to OLAD and hopefully they will be translated soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I hope so. If there are any problems on that, I would like to be informed. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: On the assumption that most of the documents have been handed over already, and that it is imminent that the rest will be forthcoming, the decision of the 10th of February states that the translation should be served on the Prosecution and filed with the Appeals Chamber within seven days of today, which means that the date due is Monday, 12th of April. This is also your understanding, Mr. Lukic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Only I will work closely with the people from OLAD to finalise these eight documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. So as far as I'm concerned, I look forward to receiving from the Prosecution and from the Defence your respective documents. Finally, I would like to mention that on April 1, the Prosecution filed a status report regarding the outstanding issues of disclosure. In that report, the Prosecution says that the disclosed materials to Mr. Stakic in January and in March 2004, and that it has completed the reviewing post-judgement material and determined that it does not contain any exculpatory material. However, as investigations are ongoing in other related cases concerning the municipality of Prijedor, the Prosecution will continue to conduct Rule 68 reviews of any material that comes into its possession as a result of those investigations. May I ask the Prosecution to give us an indication as to when those investigations might be completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is difficult to give an indication at this point in time because I was referring to ongoing cases which are related to the municipality of Prijedor. For example, the Omarska 2 case, which has not been heard. So investigations will continue in that sense, and documents will come in as and when investigations are completed. We conduct review of those materials every six months, and we've just completed the six monthly review. We will conduct it again in about three months' time, and then we will determine whether they are Rule 68 material to be disclosed Your Honour. That is how we conduct our Rule 68 material. But as and when materials come in the trial teams will do the review for this case as well and will provide us with the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you any comments from the Defence on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. On the 19th of March this year, we received extracts from the interview with Ms. Biljana Plavsic. I think it would be helpful to the Defence of Mr. Stakic if we received complete transcripts from these interviews so we could determine if there is any use of these transcripts for Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's true that we have provided extracts of Mrs. Plavsic's interviews with the OTP. We provide extracts which are clearly to us Rule 68 or falling within the boundaries of Rule 68. Other parts of the interviews may not be relevant at all to this case or may not be Rule 68. That is the standard that we apply, Your Honour. Now, if counsel wishes to have the entire interview which we feel is not necessary, perhaps counsel could provide a basis as to why he feels that he needs access to the entire interview, but we only provide Rule 68 material, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. If this matter cannot be resolved in contacts between the Defence and the Prosecution, of course the Defence can submit an appropriate motion to the Court and we will consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Is there another issue which either party would wish to raise with the Court today? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. RASHID
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: If so, I would like to thank the parties to their attendance and I call these proceedings to a close. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
